model_output.score_comment_short: The internship shows relevant tools, but most bullets leave the work unexplained.
model_output.score_comment_long: The Tableau dashboard and survey cleaning connect analytics tools to actual assignments. Most bullets stop before saying what the reports, dashboard, or findings covered. Adding those details to the internship section would make the experience easier to assess.
model_output.score_plain: A reviewer can see relevant entry-level analytics work, but may struggle to distinguish your contributions from a list of tasks. More detail about the work itself would give them a better basis for comparison.
model_output.first_impression: Your analytics internship is easy to spot, with Excel, SQL, and Tableau named in the work. The dashboard's marketing audience is worth keeping because it shows who the work was for.
model_output.biggest_gap_example: "Presented findings to the team at the end of the internship" does not say what you found, so a reviewer cannot tell what you learned from the analysis.
model_output.summary: Your Data Analytics Intern role combines reporting, survey data cleaning, and a dashboard for marketing. Alongside the B.S. in Information expected in May 2027, it positions you for internship-level analytics work. The resume names the tools, but not the questions the analysis addressed, which makes it difficult to understand the substance of your assignments.
strengths: The survey bullet names both Excel and SQL, connecting those skills to a concrete data-cleaning assignment.
Weekly reporting gives a reader a sense of the recurring work you assisted with during the internship.
The treasurer role adds budget and reimbursement responsibilities alongside your analytics work.
gaps: The Tableau bullet doesn't say what the dashboard displayed, leaving its usefulness to marketing unclear.
The survey bullet doesn't describe the data issues you handled or the cleaning steps you took, so your technical contribution is difficult to assess.
The treasurer entry doesn't explain what you can decide about the budget or reimbursements, leaving the limits of that responsibility unclear.
